findings.title: Negative flusher_processes disables flushing and backpressure silently
findings.body: `max_processes` comes from the new `--flusher-processes` click option with `type=int` and no range validation. `SpanFlusher` first does `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so `0` becomes "all shards", but a negative value survives to line 60 where `min(negative, len(shards))` returns a negative number. `range(negative)` then produces an empty `process_to_shards_map`, so no flusher processes or per-process buffers are created. `submit()` still accepts messages: the backpressure and Redis-memory checks iterate over empty `process_backpressure_since` and `self.buffers` collections, so spans continue to be written to Redis while nothing flushes them. This can fill Redis and lead to data loss/consumer failure. Add validation such as `click.IntRange(min=1)` and handle `0` explicitly.

findings.title: join(timeout) can return while later flusher processes are still running
findings.body: In `join`, after `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the deadline, the loop over `self.processes` sees `remaining_time <= 0` and executes `break`, skipping termination for the current and all remaining processes. Only processes iterated before the deadline expires are terminated. Because `close()` intentionally leaves flusher processes running until `join()`, this can leave an old generation of flusher processes alive after rebalance, concurrently flushing shards that may now be assigned to a new consumer and producing duplicate buffered segments.

findings.title: Inserting flusher_processes before produce_to_pipe breaks positional callers
findings.body: `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` previously accepted `produce_to_pipe` as the sixth positional argument. The new `flusher_processes` parameter is inserted before it, so any existing caller that constructs the factory with `produce_to_pipe` positionally now binds it to `flusher_processes`. The factory then passes the callable to `SpanFlusher` as `max_processes`, where `min(callable, int)` raises a `TypeError` during process count calculation. New parameters should be added after existing ones, or made keyword-only, to preserve the existing call contract.

findings.title: Production multiprocessing flusher path is not tested
findings.body: Both tests pass `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, which makes `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards` create `threading.Thread` instances instead of the production `mp_context.Process` path with `run_with_initialized_sentry(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer)`. The new test only asserts that two thread objects are created and that shards are distributed; it does not submit spans or verify that flushing works across processes. As a result, multiprocess-specific behavior such as pickling the per-shard buffer, process restart/health handling, and `join`/terminate behavior in real spawned processes is not exercised.
